title: Board room and corporate jargon
objectives: Recognise common corporate jargon and its plain meaning
Translate jargon into clear executive language
Avoid jargon that obscures risk or decisions
Defend a recommendation in plain language to a board

sources.title: Corporate jargon and plain language guidance

verificationNotes: Jargon lists are illustrative and drawn from common usage, not a single authoritative source.
Plain-language rewrites are Original Academy material.

sections.heading: Why jargon matters
sections.body: Jargon can signal membership and speed up expert discussion, but it often hides uncertainty, risk and decision ownership. In a board room, unclear language leads to unclear decisions. A CTO should be able to switch from expert shorthand to plain language on demand.

sections.heading: Common phrases and plain meanings
sections.body: Synergy: working together. Leverage: use. Bandwidth: capacity. Move the needle: make a measurable difference. Circle back: return to the topic. Take this offline: discuss separately. Single source of truth: one authoritative data set. Boil the ocean: attempt too much. Low-hanging fruit: easy wins. The phrase is not the problem; the missing number, owner or date is.

sections.heading: Jargon as a risk
sections.body: Jargon becomes dangerous when it replaces evidence. 'We will leverage synergies to move the needle' says nothing about cost, time or owner. Boards need decisions, trade-offs and measures. Translate every abstract phrase into a concrete ask, number and date.

sections.heading: Plain-language rules
sections.body: Prefer short sentences, active voice and concrete nouns. Name the decision, the owner, the cost and the date. Define technical terms on first use. Avoid acronyms unless everyone shares them. If a phrase cannot be rewritten plainly, the idea may not be clear yet.

workedExample.title: Rewriting a board update (illustrative)
workedExample.body:
Jargon version: 'We are leveraging cloud synergies to optimise our digital transformation and move the needle on operational excellence.'

Plain version: 'We are moving three systems to one cloud provider. This should cut hosting cost by 15 percent and reduce recovery time from 24 hours to 4 hours. Total cost is 120,000 over six months. I recommend approval; the main risk is migration delay.'

misconceptions: Thinking plain language is less professional.
learn.explainTask: In 120 words or fewer, explain a technical decision to a board in plain language.

knowledgeCheck.question: Which phrase is clearest for a board update?
options: We will reduce hosting cost by 15 percent
knowledgeCheck.why: A specific percentage is clearer than abstract jargon.

knowledgeCheck.question: Jargon becomes risky when it:
knowledgeCheck.why: Jargon is risky when it hides the real decision, cost, owner or date.

knowledgeCheck.question: A good plain-language update should include:
knowledgeCheck.why: Boards need the decision, owner, cost and date.

knowledgeCheck.question: Which is the best rewrite of 'take this offline'?
options: Discuss it separately after the meeting
knowledgeCheck.why: 'Take this offline' means discuss it separately.

knowledgeCheck.question: Acronyms should be:
options: Defined on first use unless shared
knowledgeCheck.why: Define acronyms unless the audience shares them.

build.business: Cretek presents to a board that includes non-technical members. Clear language improves decisions and accountability.
build.problem: Build a jargon-to-plain-language translator and apply it to three real board or executive updates.
requirements: Collect at least 20 jargon phrases with plain meanings
Rewrite three real updates in plain language
Include decision, owner, cost and date in each rewrite
Build a small translator or glossary tool with tests
constraints: Do not remove necessary technical detail, translate it
Must run locally with one command
build.design: Write a one-page communication standard for Cretek executive updates.
acceptance: Three rewrites include decision, owner, cost and date
build.deliverable: Glossary, three rewritten updates, glossary tool with tests, and communication standard, referenced by path.

defend.scenario: The board complains that technical updates are hard to follow and asks for clearer communication.
prompts: Why does jargon cause poor decisions?
How will you make updates clearer?
What will each update now include?
How do you balance precision with simplicity?

rubric.criterion: Updates include decision, owner, cost and date
A practical communication standard is proposed
